focus: The test and canary cluster: jev-transport-single deferral, LIVE_CORPUS_SIZE 80 vs 86, manifest tests 26/16
noveltyJustification: Five new findings: the stale canary in the wrong hub with its successor in cli-classifier, the run-confirmed admission failure at 86 vs 80, the identified 6-vs-7-hub pin behind the manifest failures, the shared count-drift mechanism, and the accepted-failure practice without an owner or expiry.
keyQuestions: Q5: What are the root causes of the open test and canary issues: the jev-transport-single canary deferral, the compiled-route-admission LIVE_CORPUS_SIZE 80 pin against 86 scenarios, and the manifest test failures?
answeredQuestions: Q5: What are the root causes of the open test and canary issues: the jev-transport-single canary deferral, the compiled-route-admission LIVE_CORPUS_SIZE 80 pin against 86 scenarios, and the manifest test failures?
ruledOut: A cross-suite registry binding pinned counts to their owning lists - three literals are cheaper to fix directly and the registry would have no caller once fixed
Running the manifest suite with a redirected sandbox to enumerate all 16 failures - the sandbox root is hardcoded and the suite can touch live serving paths; recorded as the confirming step instead

label: jev-transport-single defers because it is a stale case in the wrong hub: it expects route/single to cli-jev, but the transport axis moved to the cli-classifier hub (mode-registry comment); an in-memory run of the fixture's own evaluation returns action defer, reason no-match, and the cli-classifier fixture already carries the same prompt as jev-choice-single. Smallest fix: delete the one stale case.

The compiled-route-admission test fails exactly one test: LIVE_CORPUS_SIZE is pinned at 80 while the live gold corpus is 86 (sk-code 1, system-deep-loop 25, mcp-tooling 16, cli-external 10, cli-classifier 4, sk-doc 26, sk-design 4); a read-only run reports tests 29, pass 28, fail 1 with actual 86 expected 80. Smallest fix: set the constant to 86 and rerun the baseline report the comment requires.

The manifest tests' 16 failures have an identified sufficient cause: the suite pins all 6 hubs resolve at seven sites while the sync CLI derives from a 7-entry HUBS list including sk-design; the test file is unchanged since 2026-09-20 and sk-design became the seventh hub on 2026-09-22, so these have failed since then, independent of the epic, matching the recorded 26 pass / 16 fail over 42 tests. Smallest fix: match all \d+ hubs, the shape the CLI already prints.

The three failures share one producing mechanism: literals that pin a count or membership of a growing set owned by another file, with nothing keeping them in step. The hub set grew 6 to 7, the corpus 80 to 86, and a destination moved between hubs; the repo already derives these values elsewhere (the sync message uses HUBS.length), so this is consumer drift, not a missing capability. Smallest fix: fix the three consumers to derive from their owners; add no meta-checker.

The accepted-failure practice let the stale canary survive: the merge record lists the canary failure as existing beside otherwise-green verification with no owner or expiry, while the compiled-route guard has a printed-expiry exemption mechanism for excused hubs; canary cases have no such discipline. Smallest fix: when a known failure is named in a commit or log, name its owner and fix in the same line.
